subject: [PATCH v2] mm: page_alloc: make defrag_mode retries follow the promoted order

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author is addressing a concern about the patch's testing and review process, suggesting to keep cc:stable but only submit it to Linus for v7.4-rc1 after it has been battle-tested in the fleet.
reviews.raw_body:
I think defrag_mode is not widely used. Maybe only in Meta.

By the time we would have the patch battle-tested in the fleet.

  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer Usama Arif suggested resetting the retry counters only when the work order was actually promoted, to prevent movable requests and high-order requests from getting additional retries.
reviews.raw_body:
Should these counters be reset only when the work order was actually
promoted?

For movable requests, and requests already at or above pageblock
order, `reclaim_order == order`. Their retry budget was therefore
spent on the request itself rather than on promoted pageblock
production. Resetting the counters here can give those requests
another 17 no-progress reclaim attempts, plus additional
compaction-success retries, before OOM or allocation failure.

How about:
	if (reclaim_order != order) {
		no_progress_loops = 0;
		compaction_retries = 0;
	}

instead?

2026-10-07.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of page allocation in defrag_mode to make retries follow the promoted order, rather than the original request order. This change is intended to prevent indefinite retrying by requests that are not movable, which can lead to high memory pressure and OOM killing. The patch also updates the retry logic for direct reclaim and compaction to take into account the promoted order, and resets the retry counters when a fallback attempt is made. As a result of this change, the number of should_reclaim_retry() calls and peak memory pressure are significantly reduced, leading to improved system performance.
